name: Stance categories
description: Every person is classified pro / hostile / neutral / yellowflag / redflag. 'pro' = ally (explicit or by team-alignment judgment). 'hostile' = actively anti-Israel/antisemitic. 'neutral' = no clear lean or genuinely mixed. See flag rules for yellow/red.

name: Alliance Score (1-100)
description: Team-alignment intensity independent of the stance category. A rock-solid pro can be 95; a coalition-of-convenience pro can be 55. Lets us rank within 'pro' rather than treating all allies as equal. Backfilled from stance as a starting point, refined per-entry.

name: Team-alignment judgment
description: Coalition allies against the left generally count as 'pro' even without an explicit pro-Israel statement, per Andy's qualified judgment. Someone can be mildly critical of Israel or the Iran war and still be 'on our team,' especially united against the left. Applied to New Right / conservative-media figures (Rufo, Lindsay, Keeperman, Alex Clark, etc.).

name: Silent-majority principle
description: Business professionals and leaders generally will NOT post publicly about Israel, Judaism, or antisemitism -- that's normal professional behavior, not a negative signal. Absence of public statements is expected for business figures and must not lower their score. (Contrast: for MEDIA figures who talk politics constantly, silence on Israel is more meaningful.)

name: Philosemitic / institutional-proximity signal
description: Evidence doesn't have to be Israel-specific. Amplifying Jewish talent, Yeshiva University / RIETS credentials, Tikvah or Hertog Foundation fellowships, shared institutional homes with confirmed allies (Manhattan Institute, etc.), or writing warmly about Jewish institutional life all count as real positive signal. (John Hood spotlighting Josh Appel; Appel, Shapiro, Cost, Guerra.)

name: Enemy-of-my-enemy CAUTION
description: A shared enemy (e.g., feuding with a known antisemite) is a LEAD to investigate, NOT proof of alliance. Verify the actual reason before scoring. Example: the Cernovich/Marjorie Taylor Greene feud was about her congressional resignation, not antisemitism -- so it is NOT evidence of a pro-Israel stance despite surface appeal.

name: Circumstantial signals = leads, not verdicts
description: Guilt/innocence-by-association, secondhand claims, and shared-affiliation hunches are surfaced as leads worth checking, but are verified against documented evidence before becoming a stance call. (Corrected the 'Justin/Deconstruction Zone is Noahide' claim and the Messi 'pro-Israel' viral claim this way.)

name: Firsthand knowledge = primary source
description: For people in Andy's own network (LinkedIn connections, personal acquaintances), Andy's firsthand knowledge -- fraternal/organizational affiliations, directly observed behavior -- is treated as a primary source, often stronger than public-record search. (Dustin Tropp: AEPi chapter president, Groyper-filtering.)

name: Suggested Follow-Up Research field
description: Entries can carry an explicit 'to research' note for open questions a human should resolve manually, rendered as an amber flag on the card. Keeps unknowns visible instead of buried.

name: Data provenance / ethics
description: Do NOT bulk-extract gated or licensed databases (Start-Up Nation Central Finder, etc.). Permitted sources: open web, firsthand knowledge, government/public promotion material, and brief attributed excerpts where a license explicitly allows (Claw & Talon). Selection/curation must originate from open research or Andy's judgment, not from reproducing a protected compilation.

name: Yellow flag
description: Genuinely mixed / complicated signal worth monitoring rather than writing off -- NOT clear hostility. Says supportive things but undercuts in practice, or has a real but contested record. (Steve Bannon, Mike Cernovich, Floyd Mayweather.)

name: Red flag
description: A conduct/safety/criminal issue, independent of Israel stance. Association would damage BFT credibility regardless of the person's pro-Israel content. This is NOT a stance judgment -- it's a reputational/safety exclusion. (Tommy Robinson, David Wood.)

name: Network: Influencer / Media
description: Media personalities, commentators, podcasters, journalists, public intellectuals, creators. Silence on Israel IS informative here (they talk politics for a living). Tracked in the Influencer tab with network = 'Media/Influencer'.

name: Network: Business
description: Founders, executives, investors, operators. Silent-majority principle applies -- judged on affiliations, associations, and firsthand knowledge rather than public posts. Tracked with network = 'Business' (people) and in the Organizations / Israeli Tech tabs (entities).

name: Network: Grassroots
description: Rank-and-file supporters, activists, and audiences identified by affiliation/behavior signals (e.g., follows Libs of TikTok, attends CUFI events) rather than individual prominence. Tracked with network = 'Grassroots'.

name: Network: Entertainment
description: Entertainment-celebrity figures whose platform is cultural rather than political, with subcategories: Sports, Music, Film, TV & Media. Outsized reach to non-political audiences. Tracked with network = 'Entertainment' + a subcategory. (Sophie Cunningham, John Rocker, LeBron, Messi -> Sports; Nicki Minaj, Bieber -> Music; Paris Berelc -> Film.)

name: Rubio-vs-Vance preference weighting
description: Proxy for GOP-wing alignment. RUBIO preference (hawkish, pro-Israel-alliance wing) = POSITIVE signal, lean pro. VANCE preference (America-First / restraint wing) = a CAUTION signal to weigh, not disqualifying. Counts BOTH explicit statements AND evidenced indicators: publicly allying with, working for, being endorsed by, or associating with Rubio's core allies, friends, family, institutions, companies, staff, donors, and partners is treated as a proxy Rubio-preference signal even without a direct quote. Investigate the associational graph, don't wait for an explicit endorsement.

name: Connected to Sun Valley Policy Forum
description: Affiliation with the Sun Valley Policy Forum is a positive network signal worth adding and researching.

name: Connected to Creative Community for Peace
description: Creative Community for Peace mobilizes the entertainment industry against cultural boycotts of Israel (anti-BDS). Any affiliation is a strong pro signal, especially for entertainment/creative figures.

name: Posted positively about Sen. Lindsey Graham
description: Positive public posting about Lindsey Graham (a leading pro-Israel hawk) is a proxy signal for pro-Israel-alliance alignment. Investigate and lean pro.

name: Uses 'Judeo-Christian' positively/neutrally
description: Using the term 'Judeo-Christian' in a positive or neutral connotation signals alignment with the shared-heritage framing at the core of BFT's mission. A soft but meaningful inclusion signal.

name: Featured by The Genesis Prize Foundation
description: Anyone featured, honored, or platformed by The Genesis Prize Foundation is a strong pro-Israel/Jewish-community signal -- add and lean pro.

name: Follows Libs of TikTok
description: Following Libs of TikTok is a grassroots-level right-alignment signal. Such followers are filed to the Grassroots network as rank-and-file coalition members.

name: Connected to Advancing American Freedom
description: Advancing American Freedom (Mike Pence's org, pro-Israel policy positions) affiliation is a positive signal -- add and research the connection.

name: Associated with a16z / Founders Fund
description: Andreessen Horowitz and Founders Fund are the anchor 'Tech Right' VC firms with heavy pro-Israel and pro-West orientation. Associates are added to the Business network and researched.

name: RealLindellTV / CUFI-summit alignment
description: Part of Mike Lindell's RealLindellTV network, or appearance at the CUFI (Christians United for Israel) Summit, is a positive coalition-alignment signal.

name: Connected to Jerry Falwell Jr.
description: Connection to Jerry Falwell Jr. (Liberty University network, historically strongly pro-Israel evangelical) is a positive signal to add and research.

name: Ally-expansion rule
description: When an ally is VERIFIED, also capture their surrounding graph as leads: current company, past companies, key connections, friendly interviewers/interviewees, friends, and family. Each becomes a candidate entry or research note -- allies are nodes, not endpoints.

name: Ally links rule
description: When an ally is ADDED, record all their internet/social links (X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Facebook, Truth Social, personal sites) in the Links field so outreach and monitoring never have to re-find them.

name: Organizations vs Businesses split
description: Entities are split into two tabs: ORGANIZATIONS (NGOs, nonprofits, think tanks, universities, media outlets, campus networks) and BUSINESSES (companies, VC firms, the ally B2B/commerce network, government trade bodies). People in business roles carry network='Business' in the Influencer tab.

name: Anti-Muslim rhetoric NOT auto-flagged
description: Per Andy's direction (Jul 2026), anti-Muslim rhetoric alone is NOT grounds for a yellow/red flag; affected entries (Robert Spencer, Amy Mek) reclassified pro with documented context retained in evidence. Conduct/criminal/safety flags are unchanged (Tommy Robinson's red flag stands on convictions and conduct, not rhetoric).

name: Evidence-links rule
description: When possible, attach LINKS to the concrete evidence behind an ideological classification -- e.g., the specific social-media post and its sentiment toward allies/adversaries, a voting record, an interview clip, an org bio. Stored in the Links / evidence / source fields. Goal: make each stance/score auditable back to a source (the Liberty Score principle -- decomposable and clickable, not a gestalt).

name: Ally org/company rule
description: When an ally is added, also add the organizations and companies they lead/found/work for as their own entries (Organizations or Businesses tab), linked via the Related field. Extends the ally-expansion rule from people to institutions so the Ecosystem Network graph captures the full org web. (Backfill for existing allies is an ongoing manual-investigation task.)

name: Manual-investigation queue
description: When an entry needs human follow-up (unverified identity, thin profile, a bulk source to process, a merge to confirm), flag it in the Suggested Follow-Up Research field (amber card note) AND track it as a to-do. Bulk sources awaiting processing are logged on their hub entry (e.g., IAF Top-50 2021-2024 on the Israel Allies Foundation entry). Do NOT fabricate entries to clear a queue -- stage them honestly.

name: Bulk-source manual-investigation queue (open)
description: OPEN QUEUE (as of Jul 2026): (1) IAF 'Israel's Top 50 Christian Allies' for 2024, 2023, 2022, 2021, and the original edition -- process, dedup, add net-new [2025 DONE]. (2) Systematic org/company backfill for all previously-added allies per the Ally org/company rule. (3) Verify flagged unknowns: Hyun-bo Son, Jeremy Ballinger, Pastor Troy Jackson, Pastor Carlos Luna, Pastor Jacques Kangudia, Carlos Duran (Hombres de Palabra) merge-check.

name: Criticism of Graham / Cruz = yellow flag
description: Public criticism of Senators Lindsey Graham or Ted Cruz (leading pro-Israel-alliance hawks) is a CAUTION signal indicating the America-First/restraint wing -- yellow-flag and monitor rather than treat as pro. The mirror image of the Rubio-preference positive signal. (Andrew Kolvet, Blake Neff / the post-Kirk Charlie Kirk Show.)

name: Enemy vs. Rival distinction
description: Distinguish ENEMIES (actively hostile to Jews/Israel -- Fuentes, Candace Owens, Joel Webbon) from RIVALS (compete for the same audience/coalition space but are not hostile -- rival conservative outlets, competing pastors, other GOP factions). BOTH transitive rules apply: enemy-of-my-enemy = friend, AND rival-of-my-rival = friend. A rival of our rival is a recruitment target, not a threat. This REFINES (does not replace) the enemy-of-my-enemy CAUTION rule -- still verify the actual reason for the conflict before scoring (the Cernovich/MTG feud was about her resignation, not antisemitism).

name: Voluntary vs. paid anti-antisemitism advocacy
description: BOOST non-Jewish voices who speak against antisemitism/anti-Zionism VOLUNTARILY over those who likely did so as a paid engagement. Voluntary indicators (score UP): said it on their OWN platform unprompted; on a non-Jewish/secular platform; to a hostile or indifferent audience; at personal or professional cost; unsolicited on social media. Paid/prompted indicators (discount): keynote at a Jewish-org gala, sponsored content, honorarium events, appearances where the ask was the occasion. Rationale: voluntary advocacy on their own turf proves conviction AND reaches new audiences; a paid speech to an already-convinced room proves neither. (Seth Dillon attacking Tucker/Candace on his own platform = voluntary, scored 92.)

name: Claude proactive-addition rule
description: Claude should PROACTIVELY add people/orgs meeting our criteria by connecting the dots -- not only names Andy supplies -- with justification + evidence, marking provenance in the Added By field (Andy / Claude (proactive) / Collaborator). Everything added before Jul 2026 is stamped Added By = Andy. Proactive adds still meet the evidence bar: no fabrication; unverifiable ones get flagged, not invented.

name: Connection-yield tracking
description: Every entity card shows: (a) AUTO-COUNTED ally links -- how many other tracked entities it connects to, computed from the same edge logic as the Ecosystem Network graph; (b) Yield Status -- Untapped / Partially mined / Well mined / Exhausted; (c) Remaining potential -- what else is reachable through that node. Purpose: make it visible which allies are unmined leads vs. fully worked, so expansion is targeted rather than random.

name: Backlog maintenance (standing rule)
description: Any request that is blocked, partial, unbounded, unverifiable, or declined MUST be logged in the Backlog/To-Do tab with the reason and the concrete next step -- never silently dropped. This prevents invisible misses: a Jul 2026 audit found 6 explicit asks never added, and 80 orgs named in evidence with no entry.

name: Nationality ranking: American allies rank highest
description: RANK ORDER for influencer value: (1) AMERICAN natives who support Israel = highest -- the international world perceives Israeli and Jewish advocates as self-interested, so American non-Jewish/native voices carry the most persuasive weight; (2) allies from nations CLOSE to America (UK, Canada, Australia...) -- soft-ranked by how close that country is to the US; (3) other internationals; (4) ISRAELIS rank LOWEST as influencers, because international audiences discount them as biased. THIS IS NOT A HARD RULE -- see the influence-override clause. Andy and collaborators retain full control of any ranking.

name: Influence overrides nationality (override clause)
description: CHARISMA, INTELLIGENCE, and ACTUAL INFLUENCE are the GREATEST factors and OVERRIDE the nationality ranking. Andy and collaborators have full manual control of every score. Canonical example: Ollie Anisfeld (J-TV) is British AND Jewish -- doubly discounted by nationality -- but is charismatic, intelligent, media-savvy, good-looking, and fluent in both politics and theology, so he ranks high anyway (further helped by J-TV's largest audience being American). Nationality is a tiebreaker, not a ceiling.

name: Israeli-content rule: mine the graph, not the reach
description: For ISRAELI influencers, the value is less their own (discounted) persuasive reach than their GRAPH. What to look for in Israeli creators' content: WHO ARE THEIR FRIENDS -- who they host, who they collaborate with, who they comment on positively. Those relationships surface non-Israeli (ideally American, ideally non-Jewish) allies who rank higher than the Israeli creator themselves. Treat Israeli accounts as discovery instruments.

name: B2B network inclusion criteria
description: INCLUDE in the Business/B2B network any company or capital-management firm (VC, PE, growth equity, real estate, etc.) meeting ANY of: (a) has offices in Israel; (b) is invested in Israeli companies; (c) has a Jewish and/or Zionist and/or Evangelical and/or devout Protestant founder, president, CEO, chairman, vice president, or majority investor/stakeholder; (d) has acquired an Israeli company. Note the silent-majority principle applies -- these are structural/affiliation signals, and no public Israel statement is expected from a business.

name: Audience geography >= influencer nationality
description: MAP AUDIENCE GEOGRAPHY -- where the audience actually IS matters as much as, if not MORE than, the influencer's own nationality. A foreign influencer with a large AMERICAN audience delivers American persuasion; an American influencer whose audience is entirely overseas does not. This REFINES the nationality ranking: nationality is a weak proxy, audience geography is the real variable it was proxying for. Canonical case: Ollie Anisfeld is British and Jewish (doubly discounted by nationality) but J-TV's LARGEST AUDIENCE IS AMERICAN -- so his effective value is far higher than his passport implies. Record this in the Audience Geography field on every influencer.

name: Posted positively about Joshua Baer
description: Anyone who publicly posted POSITIVELY about Joshua Baer (Jewish Zionist founder/CEO of Capital Factory, killed in a plane crash 17 Jun 2026) is a candidate for the Business-leader and B2B network map -- along with their companies. Rationale: public tribute to a Jewish Zionist figure is a voluntary, self-initiated philosemitic signal from exactly the silent-majority business class that never posts about Israel directly. TIME-BOUNDED and high-yield: memorial posts cluster in the weeks after Jun 2026. First pass already yielded Jason Calacanis, Bill Gurley, Thom Singer, Jonathan Greenblatt, Ted Cruz (tracked), Bryan Chambers (tracked), Lloyd Doggett. NOTE: full enumeration needs social-listening tooling -- these came from published tribute coverage only.

name: Hyperlinked-source requirement
description: Every claim should carry a CLICKABLE, credible source a human can verify -- not just a publication name and date. Sources and links render in a collapsible 'Sources & links' dropdown on each card (collapsed by default to avoid clutter). Entries with NO clickable source are auto-flagged with an amber warning on that dropdown. AUDIT (Jul 2026): 315 of 439 entities (72%) had no clickable URL -- mostly inherited from the original _5 seed file, which cited things like 'Jerusalem Post, Sep 2025'. Re-sourcing those is a tracked Backlog item. GOING FORWARD: no entry is added without a clickable source or an explicit unverified flag.

name: Audience demographics (sourced only)
description: Record audience demographics (age, gender, political lean, faith, geography) in the Audience Demographics field -- but ONLY from real sourced data (published reporting, Comscore/Nielsen/Pew figures, platform-disclosed stats), never invented. Claude does NOT have access to audience analytics; a full demographic pass across the network requires paid tooling (SparkToro, Audiense, Similarweb, Comscore). Any inference must be explicitly marked as inference. Rationale: fabricated demographics would look authoritative and quietly corrupt targeting decisions -- worse than an empty field.

name: Jews should NOT be publicly front-facing
description: STRATEGIC PRINCIPLE from BFT board member Dana Gibber (interview, verbatim): 'having Jews publicly involved is not great actually... it should be an organic and internal effort of the Christian community to step into the light and be much more vocal and assertive about their views.' Jewish involvement stays behind the scenes; the public voice must be authentically Christian or the whole effort reads as astroturf and the 'Jews pulling the strings' accusation lands. Exception: a small handful of semi-public figures like Johnnie Moore. CONSEQUENCE FOR SCORING: American, non-Jewish, authentically Christian voices are the scarce, high-value asset -- this is the deeper reason behind the nationality ranking and the voluntary-advocacy rule, not merely optics.

name: Asymmetric strategy: humor beats fact-checking
description: JOHNNIE MOORE (interview, verbatim): 'disinformation... is not actually about the facts. It's about community. It's about who you trust and what you believe and what community you feel a part of.' 'These sorts of asymmetric strategies are what we're missing in this whole thing.' He credits the BABYLON BEE with ~30% more success than anyone else simply by being funny and smart. IMPLICATION: comedians, satirists, and culture/meme accounts are STRATEGIC ASSETS, not light entertainment -- score them accordingly. Fact-checking is necessary hygiene but does not win. (Validates Seth Dillon 92, Ami Kozak 87; argues for actively recruiting more comedy/culture talent.)

name: Podcast gap: leg-1 concrete target
description: JOHNNIE MOORE's explicit, concrete leg-1 ask: evangelicals UNDER-INDEX in podcasting while Catholics and libertarians OVER-INDEX. He wants to 'immediately find 20 folks who have significant audiences [but are] just not there, and move them into that space.' TARGET PROFILE: has real audience + evangelical + NOT currently podcasting. This is a named deliverable, not a vague goal -- flag every candidate who fits and track toward 20.

name: Grassroots community = bottom-up tactics
description: JOHNNIE MOORE: the evangelical community is GRASSROOTS and bottom-up -- 'very much like a free market.' No leader can endorse something and cascade it downward (upside: no single point of failure; downside: momentum is hard to create). It is HIGH-TRUST, so once momentum exists it is 'super high leverage.' CONSEQUENCE: do not over-weight formal titles/hierarchy. A megachurch's influential lay attorney may matter more than a denominational officer -- which is exactly why Johnnie wants strategic LAY MEMBERS mapped, not just clergy.

name: [UNBUILT] Strategic-cities lay-member database
description: JOHNNIE MOORE DESCRIBED A DATABASE WE HAVE NOT BUILT. His vision: (1) pick ~20 STRATEGIC CITIES worldwide (Sao Paulo, Santiago, Brussels, Geneva...); (2) map the LARGE CHURCHES in each; (3) identify the strategic LAY MEMBERS/ATTENDEES -- 'what no one has done before' -- top attorneys, doctors, school-board members, NOT the clergy; (4) index them BY SECTOR (education, law, medicine, safety) for RAPID ACTIVATION. Use case: an antisemitic incident in Chile -> you already know an aligned attorney attends a large church there who could be pro bono counsel. His Oct-8 lament: had we reached strategic allies across 5-7 sectors that afternoon, we could have countered the street mobilization. He expects to hire regional researchers (South America, Africa). CURRENT DATABASE IS: US-centric, media-influencer-centric, public-figure-centric. HIS VISION IS: global, church-based, lay-professional, sector-indexed. Complementary but different -- this is the biggest strategic gap in the project.

name: Seed-100 portfolio model
description: ANDY'S STRATEGY (Jul 2026), and the right answer to BFT's donors: do NOT try to pick the perfect 20 up front. SEED ~100 untapped/undiscovered influencers, measure who performs, then BACK THE WINNERS. This is venture logic -- exactly how BFT's founders (Rad/Weir/Broukhim/Duel) already think -- and it answers the donor objection ('we put money into evangelicals and did not see returns') far better than a hand-picked list: it makes returns MEASURABLE and concentrates spend only on proven performers. Pipeline stages tracked in Seed Stage: Candidate -> Seeded -> Performing -> Backed (or Dropped). Baseline Audience is captured at seed time so growth is measurable, not asserted.

name: Leg-1 target profile: audience WITHOUT a podcast
description: Johnnie Moore's exact ask: evangelicals under-index in podcasting while Catholics/libertarians over-index; find people who ALREADY have significant audiences but are NOT in that space, and move them into it. Operationalized as the Podcast Status field -- 'No podcast (TARGET)' marks the profile. KEY INSIGHT: the hard part is not building an audience, it is MOVING an existing audience into a format they do not yet occupy -- which is why an established 4M-follower TikToker with no podcast beats a nobody with a microphone. As of Jul 2026 the database already contained 60 such candidates.

name: Audience numbers must be LIVE-VERIFIED
description: AUDIT FINDING (14 Jul 2026): audience figures taken from articles/bios/wikis are stale or wrong. Live checks found Dave Rubin at 3.22M (recorded: 2M+), Ollie Anisfeld/J-TV at 449K (recorded: 250K, from a Jerusalem Post piece), Goldie Ghamari at 436K TikTok + 221K YouTube (recorded: no number), and Lance Johnston at 2,148 TikTok followers vs a recorded '100K+ TikTok' -- WRONG BY ~50x, sourced from EverybodyWiki. WHAT IS FETCHABLE: YouTube (subs, views, join date) and TikTok (followerCount). WHAT IS NOT: X/Twitter (JS-rendered), Instagram (not trivially parseable), Social Blade (403). RULE: record the handle in Links, run tools/refresh_audience.py, and stamp Audience Verified with the date. Audience size drives the seed-100 'back the winners' model -- it must be measured, not asserted. NEVER cite an unvetted wiki for a follower count.

name: YouTube is a discovery channel (not just a metric source)
description: CORRECTION to an earlier stated limit: YouTube channel SEARCH is fetchable and parseable (results?search_query=...&sp=EgIQAg%3D%3D filters to channels only), returning channel names + handles + subscriber counts. So YouTube-native discovery of unknown creators IS possible -- it is not limited to bounded rosters. Caveats: query craft matters enormously (naive queries return noise), and it surfaces adversaries as well as allies. This partially closes the discovery gap for the seed-100 pass. X/Twitter discovery remains blocked.

name: Nurture / Emerging category
description: NEW TAB (Andy, Jul 2026). NURTURE holds people NOT yet confirmed pro-Israel/philosemitic but whose background suggests they likely would be IF ASKED -- plus rising talent and flip targets. Four types: (1) 'Likely ally (unasked)' -- profile fits, never asked; (2) 'Rising/emerging (<50K)' -- under 50K followers across platforms, i.e. back them BEFORE they break out (seed-100 logic one tier down); (3) 'Flip target' -- currently adverse but potentially movable; (4) 'Watch'. CRITICAL DISCIPLINE: nurture is NOT a laundering bucket. A flip target with a documented adverse signal (e.g. @Ariathome supporting Mamdani) stays RED-FLAGGED inside nurture -- 'potential flip' and 'likely ally' are different things and must not be blurred.

name: Rising/emerging threshold: <50K followers
description: ANDY'S RULE: anyone under ~50K followers across platforms goes in Nurture as Rising/Emerging rather than the main Influencer tab. Rationale: the cheapest time to build a relationship is before someone breaks out -- the same portfolio logic as seed-100, applied earlier. Graduate them to Influencers when they cross the threshold or when their alliance value is confirmed.

name: Boost: attacking Candace Owens / Tucker Carlson / Nick Fuentes / Sneako
description: BOOST anyone who publicly attacks Candace Owens, Tucker Carlson, Nick Fuentes, or Sneako -- the four named antisemitic/Israel-hostile poles of the online right (all tracked hostile here). Rationale: attacking them is a costly, voluntary act INSIDE the conservative coalition -- it invites retaliation from one's own side, so it signals conviction, not convenience. Combine with the voluntary-vs-paid rule: doing it on one's OWN platform scores highest. (Seth Dillon 92 -- called Tucker and Candace 'the two most famous antisemites'; Ami Kozak 87 -- satirizes all of them; Jamie Michell; Graham Allen.)

name: Yellow ribbon / blue square signal
description: ANDY'S RULE: anyone seen wearing the YELLOW RIBBON (Israeli hostages) or the BLUE SQUARE pin (#StandUpToJewishHate) is a positive signal -- add and lean pro. Why it is a good signal: both are cheap to omit and visible to wear, so wearing one is a small voluntary public act, especially outside Jewish spaces. LIMIT: this is a VISUAL signal in photos/video, which Claude cannot detect -- it can only be applied by a human reviewer or image-recognition tooling. Documented as a rule for humans, not something running automatically.

name: Replacement theology = structural red flag
description: Surfaced by the Doug Wilson case (Andy, Jul 2026). Someone can express support for Israel and the Jewish people while holding REPLACEMENT THEOLOGY / supersessionism -- the doctrine that the Church supersedes Israel in God's covenant. That support is structurally unstable: it is not grounded in a permanent covenant and can invert. This is the theological ROOT of the drift Johnnie Moore is fighting, so it is a red flag despite pro-sounding statements -- distinct from dispensationalist/Christian-Zionist allies whose support is covenantal. CHECK THEOLOGY, NOT JUST STATEMENTS.

name: Congressional sweep = evidence-based politics
description: CORRECTION OF A REAL GAP (14 Jul 2026): the Political tab held only 22 entries -- assembled ad hoc from Andy's LinkedIn follows and the IAF Top-50 -- and was missing obvious allies like Dan Crenshaw. FIX: legislators are now added from their ACTUAL LEGISLATIVE RECORD via the official Library of Congress API (api.congress.gov), which returns bill cosponsor rosters as clean JSON. congress.gov's website is Cloudflare-blocked (403) but the API is not; GovTrack also works. METHOD: pull cosponsor lists for major pro-Israel bills; anyone cosponsoring 2+ is added with the bills as citable evidence; original-cosponsor status is a stronger signal than late joining. This is exactly the Liberty Score principle -- a score decomposable into documented acts ('which bills, which votes') rather than judgment. LIMIT: the DEMO_KEY rate-limits after ~2 bills; a FREE api.congress.gov key would enable the full sweep across every Israel-related bill and both chambers.

name: RED LINE: voted against Israel defense funding
appliesTo: All public officials, past and present
description: Andy's rule, verbatim: 'any public official who voted against Defense funding for Israel crosses a red line.' EXECUTED 15 Jul 2026 against the primary source: House Clerk roll-call XML (clerk.house.gov/evs), 6,332 roll calls scanned 2015-2026. The two clean defense-funding tests are H.R.5323 (Iron Dome Supplemental, 23 Sep 2021, passed 420-9-2) and H.R.8034 (Israel Security Supplemental, 20 Apr 2024, passed 366-58). 60 legislators voted NO on at least one. CRITICAL: the rule may NOT be applied literally -- see the disambiguation criterion below.

name: Vote-pattern disambiguation: a single NO is NOT proof of hostility
description: THE MOST IMPORTANT METHODOLOGICAL RULE IN THE POLITICAL DATASET. Applied literally, the red-line rule flags 60 legislators. Only 13 survive scrutiny. The other 47 are deficit hawks and process voters who oppose emergency supplemental spending generally, not Israel. Proof: Chip Roy voted YEA on Iron Dome and is 90.9% pro-Israel across 30 clean votes; Jamie Raskin 95.8%; Ro Khanna 96.0%; Scott Perry 96.7%. Each voted NO once, on H.R.8034, an unoffset emergency supplemental. RULE: never red-line on a single vote. Compute the pro-Israel rate across all 30 clean votes. Under 75% = Tier 1 GENUINE (hostile). 75-90% = Tier 2 REVIEW (human call). Over 90% = Tier 3 FISCAL (do NOT red-line). Thomas Massie is the case that proves the method works: 51.7%, the ONLY Republican among the nine Iron Dome NO votes, NO again in 2024 -- the pattern separates him from every other Republican fiscal hawk.

name: Confounded votes are excluded from scoring
description: Of 55 Israel-related roll calls, only 30 are CLEAN tests where a NO vote is a real signal. EXCLUDED as confounded: H.R.7217 (Feb 2024 -- a standalone Israel bill widely read as a maneuver to kill the bipartisan Senate package; Democratic NOs were about the maneuver); H.R.6090 Antisemitism Awareness Act (First Amendment objections from BOTH left and right -- Massie, Greene, Gaetz voted no on 1A grounds); H.Res.894 (92 Democrats voted PRESENT objecting to equating anti-Zionism with antisemitism, not to condemning antisemitism); the three Tlaib censure votes (process objections from members who are themselves pro-Israel); and all rule/previous-question votes (pure party-line noise). H.Res.183 (2019) is INVERTED: its 23 NO votes were Republicans who thought the post-Omar resolution too weak -- a NO there is arguably PRO-Israel.

name: Voting records find ENEMIES; they cannot rank ALLIES
description: MEASURED FINDING, and it should shape strategy. 236 legislators have a perfect 100% record across 20+ clean Israel votes. 50 of our own 96 political entries are 100% voters, Dan Crenshaw among them at 21/21. Pro-Israel measures pass 420-9. Therefore a perfect voting record is the NORM, not a distinction -- it confirms an ally but does not differentiate one from another. All discriminating power in roll-call data is in the DEVIATIONS. Corollary: do not spend Alliance Score bandwidth on vote-based ally ranking; use votes as a disqualifier and a floor, and rank allies on reach, charisma, and willingness to spend political capital -- which is what Johnnie's 'less sentimental, more substantive' standard actually asks for.

name: Votes measure position, NOT conduct -- weight conduct higher
description: A pro-Israel voting record does NOT clear someone whose conduct is hostile. Measured examples: Paul Gosar votes 93.1% pro-Israel yet has appeared at AFPAC alongside Nick Fuentes; Matt Gaetz 94.7%; Marjorie Taylor Greene 87.5% on a lifetime average that is backloaded with older votes while her recent trajectory is sharply hostile and aligned with the Tucker/Fuentes current this project exists to counter. Roll-call data is a floor, not a clearance. Where votes and conduct diverge, WEIGHT THE CONDUCT -- it is the better predictor of where someone lands next.

name: Never keyword-search bill titles to find Israel votes
description: A hard-won lesson worth preserving. Keyword-matching Clerk vote descriptions for 'Israel'/'Iron Dome' across 6,332 roll calls returned 54 hits and MISSED THE IRON DOME VOTE ITSELF -- the most important Israel vote of the decade. The Clerk records H.R.5323 by its formal long title, 'Making supplemental appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2022', which contains neither 'Israel' nor 'Iron Dome', and the index truncates it. RULE: always cross-check keyword sweeps against a hand-curated list of known bills by NUMBER. An unknown number of Israel provisions remain hidden inside generically-titled appropriations and NDAA votes -- see the backlog.

name: Resolve legislator identity by bioguide ID, never by name
description: House Clerk XML records members by last name with state disambiguators only ('Garcia (IL)', 'Johnson (GA)'). Naive substring matching against full names produced real, dangerous collisions in this database: 'Mike Garcia' (R-CA) matched Chuy Garcia (D-IL); Speaker 'Mike Johnson' (R-LA) matched Hank Johnson (D-GA); 'Mark Green' (R-TN) matched Al Green (D-TX); 'Lance Gooden' (R-TX) matched Bob Good (R-VA). Each would have imported a hostile record onto an ally. RULE: join on the bioguide ID (the name-id attribute in Clerk XML), resolved against the unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset. Never match on name.

name: Verification means running it, not counting braces
description: Claude spent this project using brace/bracket/backtick counting as a substitute for verification, on the belief that no JavaScript engine was available. That belief was never tested and was FALSE -- macOS ships JavaScriptCore (jsc). The cost of the untested assumption: three syntax errors reached production and the live app was fully broken. Balanced braces say nothing about a broken string literal. STANDING RULE: run python3 tools/validate.py (real parse + SEED_DATA execution via jsc) before every deploy; tools/deployify.py now enforces it and aborts on failure. GENERAL PRINCIPLE, which has now cost this project twice: TEST the limit before asserting it. The same untested-assumption error previously led Claude to claim no social-platform access, when YouTube and TikTok were in fact reachable -- which had been hiding a ~50x audience error on Lance Johnston.

name: Never regex-patch JS source across quoted fields
appliesTo: All batch edits to this file
description: The pattern field:"[^"]*" is UNSAFE against this dataset and must not be used. [^"]* is blind to escaped quotes (\"), so on any entry containing an escaped quote the match runs past the field boundary and a substitution overwrites unrelated content -- silently. This is not hypothetical: it corrupted the MilkBarTV entry and broke production. 57 entries currently contain escaped quotes and are exposed to it. Prefer: parse the row, mutate the value as data, re-serialize with a real serializer (json.dumps produces valid JS string literals and handles quotes and accents correctly).

name: SOURCE HIERARCHY: primary filings first; Wikipedia is NOT acceptable
appliesTo: Every sourced claim in this database
description: Andy, 16 Jul 2026: 'you cant rely on wikipedia data it is often corrupted, especially about issues concerning Israel.' He is right, and it is DOCUMENTED, not a hunch. Wikipedia's Arbitration Committee topic-banned eight editors over Israel-Palestine editing in Jan 2025 (six pro-Palestine, two pro-Israel), and banned three others in Dec 2024 for canvassing. The ADL published 'Editing for Hate', documenting a coordinated campaign; the advocacy group Tech for Palestine recruited volunteers for systematic edits and its lead editor received an indefinite site ban. Most tellingly: Wikipedia editors voted in June 2024 to declare THE ADL ITSELF an 'unreliable source' on Israel-Palestine. Citing Wikipedia in a BFT artifact is a liability -- a donor or a hostile reader can dismiss the claim by attacking the source, and on Israel topics specifically the source is genuinely contested. REQUIRED HIERARCHY, best first: (1) PRIMARY legal/official records -- SEC EDGAR filings (data.sec.gov, free, no key, legally binding), House Clerk roll-call XML, congress.gov, court filings, official government registries; (2) the subject's OWN publication -- company IR page, official press release, the person's own post or video; (3) established outlets with named reporters and a corrections policy; (4) Wikipedia -- ONLY as a navigational aid to find a real source, NEVER as the citation itself. PROVEN 16 Jul 2026: re-sourcing Israeli Tech from Wikipedia to SEC filings did not merely swap URLs -- it CHANGED THE FACTS. Amdocs turned out to be incorporated in the United Kingdom (Guernsey), not Israel. SentinelOne and Lemonade are Delaware corporations. JFrog and Taboola are Israeli-incorporated but US-headquartered. None of that was visible from the Wikipedia summaries.

name: Israeli Tech category rule: incorporation vs HQ vs founders
description: RESOLVED FROM SEC PRIMARY FILINGS, 16 Jul 2026 -- the category was previously implicit and therefore wrong in places. The filings report TWO distinct legal facts, and they disagree more often than expected. ISRAELI-INCORPORATED AND ISRAEL-HQ (9): Check Point, NICE, Tower Semiconductor, Fiverr, Cellebrite, Playtika, Global-e, Similarweb, Nova. ISRAELI-INCORPORATED BUT US-HQ (2): JFrog (Sunnyvale), Taboola (New York). NOT ISRAELI-INCORPORATED (4): Amdocs (United Kingdom/Guernsey), SolarEdge (Delaware, but HQ Herzliya), SentinelOne (Delaware, HQ Mountain View), Lemonade (Delaware, HQ New York). RECOMMENDATION FOR ANDY: keep all of them, but stop pretending the category is one thing. The HYBRIDS are the most strategically valuable entries here, not the impurities -- a company that is Israeli-incorporated with a US headquarters, or US-incorporated with Israeli R&D, IS the Israeli-talent/American-distribution bridge Andy described in the Johnnie interview. Index on the bridge, not on passport purity. The two exits prove the point: CyberArk into Palo Alto, Wiz into Google.

name: 'No podcast' is the WRONG filter for Johnnie's leg 1
description: Andy, 16 Jul 2026: 'Nurture is one of the most significant categories... johnnie emphasized that evangelicals are under indexing in podcasting so I think a top goal will be identifying christian zionists with long-form audio-video potential.' The existing filter (podcastStatus = 'No podcast (TARGET)', 61 people) does not survive contact with the facts, for TWO separate reasons. (1) IT IS FACTUALLY WRONG: verified against the Apple Podcasts API on 16 Jul 2026, at least 13 of the 61 ALREADY HOST ACTIVE PODCASTS -- Riley Gaines (The Riley Gaines Show, 196 eps, Fox), Ben Ferguson (2,032 eps), Brandon Tatum (The Officer Tatum Show), Nick Shirley, CJ Pearson, Jentezen Franklin (361), Allen Jackson (796), Larry Huch (553), Joni Lamb (575), Tony Perkins (201), Susan Michael (287), Laurie Cardoza-Moore, Joshua Carr (568). Handing Johnnie a 'move these people into podcasting' list led by a Fox host with 196 episodes would be humiliating. (2) IT IS CONCEPTUALLY WRONG, which matters more. Evangelicals do NOT under-index in SERMON podcasting -- that genre is saturated (Franklin 361, Jackson 796, Huch 553, Lamb 575). They under-index in CONVERSATIONAL long-form: the Rogan / Lex / Shapiro / Theo Von format. A sermon is broadcast; a podcast is conversation. Those are different skills and different products. THE FILTER SHOULD BE: proven long-form delivery + significant audience + NOT YET in conversational long-form + available. Not merely 'has no RSS feed'.

name: Long-form A/V potential: the scoring rubric
description: Rank on these, highest weight first. (1) PROVEN LONG-FORM DELIVERY -- do they already hold an audience for 30+ minutes anywhere? Sermons, lectures, streams, teaching, standup. This is the single strongest signal and the most under-exploited: A PASTOR ALREADY DELIVERS 40 MINUTES TO CAMERA EVERY WEEK, with a built-in audience. The gap is format and distribution, not ability. Johnnie came from exactly that world (Liberty). (2) CONVERSATIONAL RANGE -- can they be INTERVIEWED, not just deliver? Look for guest appearances on other shows. A preacher who cannot do dialogue will not survive the format. Wesley Huff is the proof case: his Rogan appearance was the whole breakout, and it was conversation, not preaching. (3) AUDIENCE ON THE WRONG PLATFORM -- big on TikTok/IG/X (short-form) with no long-form home. That IS the arbitrage. Allie Schnacky (4M+ TikTok) is the archetype. (4) AVAILABILITY -- this disqualifies most of the current list. A sitting Speaker of the House, a sitting Senator, an 83-year-old megachurch founder, or someone running a $700M NGO is NOT going to start a podcast. Screen for career stage: building and hungry, not established and busy. (5) US/ENGLISH AUDIENCE -- per the audience-geography criterion, which outranks nationality. The current list carries Japanese, Hungarian, Kenyan, Congolese and Latin American pastors: real allies, real networks, but not answers to 'evangelicals under-index in AMERICAN podcasting'. Keep them as allies; remove them from THIS list. (6) A 'WHY NOW' -- a book, a controversy, a viral moment, a platform shift. Podcasts launch off momentum.

name: Podcast status must be VERIFIED, never asserted
description: The Apple Podcasts search API is free, needs no key, and returns show name, host, episode count and last-release date: https://itunes.apple.com/search?media=podcast&term=NAME&country=US -- use it before tagging anyone. CAUTION, learned the hard way on 16 Jul 2026: automated name-matching FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS and cannot be trusted unattended. Loose matching produced false positives -- 'Mike Johnson' matched a cybersecurity podcast and a Baptist church, 'Tim Scott' matched a Walt Disney World fan podcast, and 'Manny Pacquiao - Audio Biography' is a show ABOUT him, not BY him. Tightening it to require the person as credited artist then produced false NEGATIVES -- it lost Riley Gaines and Ben Ferguson, because their shows are credited to FOX, not to them. There is no regex that solves this. Verify each candidate by eye. Record the show, episode count, last-release date and the date checked.

name: DORMANT beats ABSENT as a podcast target
description: A dormant podcast is a BETTER leg-1 target than no podcast at all, and this inverts the intuition. Someone who ran a show and stopped has already proven they can do it, already has a feed and back catalogue, and already built some audience -- they need a reason and backing to restart, not persuading that they are capable. Someone who never started is an unproven bet on latent ability. Verified example: Allie Schnacky hosted 'Keep It Real' (44 episodes, last 27 Jul 2025) alongside 4M+ TikTok followers. She is not a 'can she do it?' question, she is a 'why did she stop?' question -- and that is a far cheaper thing for BFT to fix. Sweep the full roster for dormant feeds; they are the cheapest wins on the board.

name: ROSTER GATES: genuine loyalty AND real talent. No quota.
description: Andy, 16 Jul 2026, correcting the framing: '20 is just a number we want as many as possible as long as they are real loyal allies of Israel/The Jews and are really talented.' SO: Johnnie's '~20' is NOT a target and must not be optimised for. It is a floor on ambition, not a cap. The list is capped only by the two GATES, which are pass/fail and non-negotiable. GATE 1 -- GENUINE LOYALTY. Not aligned, not useful, not anti-woke: LOYAL. GATE 2 -- REAL TALENT. Actually good, not merely on-side. A candidate must pass BOTH. Everything Claude previously weighted highly -- availability, US/English audience, podcast status, career stage -- is DOWNSTREAM RANKING, not a gate. A loyal, talented person who is hard to reach is still on the list; a convenient, available mediocrity is not. Scale the list as far as the gates allow.

name: GATE 1 -- Loyalty is measured by COST PAID, not by statements
appliesTo: Every ally claim in the database
description: THE UNIFYING TEST, and it already underlies several criteria Andy set separately. Statements are cheap and everyone makes them; the question is what it COST them. Costly signals cannot be faked at scale. STRONG LOYALTY SIGNALS (rank by how much it cost): spoke up when it was UNPOPULAR IN THEIR OWN MILIEU (the right's drift makes this expensive now -- Seth Dillon attacking Candace Owens and Tucker Carlson is the model, and Andy flagged it for exactly this reason); TOOK INCOMING for it -- being attacked by Tucker/Candace/Fuentes/Sneako is itself proof of cost, which is why the attack-them boost criterion exists; VOLUNTARY, NOT PAID (Andy's existing rule: an unpaid voluntary stand outranks what is likely a paid speaker engagement); SUSTAINED over years, not a single post; PRE-OCT-7 -- anyone pro-Israel BEFORE it was a live political identity is vastly more credible than a post-Oct-7 convert; PRINCIPLED/THEOLOGICAL foundation rather than transactional. OPPORTUNIST SIGNALS (fail the gate): only arrived once it paid; paid by pro-Israel institutions to say it; never takes a cost; swings with audience sentiment; anti-woke or anti-Islam but never actually PRO-Israel -- this is the 'enemy of my enemy' trap Andy explicitly warned about, and it is the commonest failure mode on this list. OPERATIONAL RULE: for every roster candidate, record WHAT IT COST THEM. If the answer is 'nothing', they have not passed Gate 1 -- they are unproven, not loyal. Unproven belongs in Nurture as a watch item, not on the roster.

name: GATE 2 -- Talent is measured by holding an audience, not by alignment
description: Andy: 'really talented'. And earlier, on ranking: 'charisma, intelligence - actual influence - should be the greatest factor - Ollie Anisfeld is a great example.' The failure mode this gate exists to prevent is the one that has sunk every previous well-funded effort in this space: a roster of people who agree with you and cannot hold an audience. Donors have already pushed back on BFT that they 'put a lot of money into evangelicals' without the returns -- an aligned-but-boring roster is precisely how that money disappeared. Alignment is the price of entry, not the product. MEASURE: (a) can they hold attention for 30+ minutes -- sermons, lectures, streams, standup all count as evidence; (b) CONVERSATIONAL RANGE -- can they be INTERVIEWED, not just deliver? Guest appearances on other people's shows are the tell, and Wesley Huff's Rogan appearance is the existence proof; (c) do they grow an audience on their own merits, not via institutional distribution; (d) charisma and humour -- Johnnie's own point that the Babylon Bee outperforms by ~30% purely by being funny and smart. Fact-checking alone loses. HARD TEST: would you watch them if you disagreed with them? If not, they fail Gate 2 no matter how loyal.

name: THE PAID-INFLUENCE THREAT vindicates the cost-paid gate
description: Source: TIME, Eric Cortellessa, 13 Jul 2026 -- 'Trump's Ex-Campaign Manager Is Running An Israeli Influence Operation Targeting the MAGA Base' (https://time.com/article/2026/07/13/brad-parscale-israel-influence-operation/). FARA filings show the ad agency Havas hired Brad Parscale's firm Clock Tower X to run a digital campaign FOR THE STATE OF ISRAEL: $1.5M/month, 100 content pieces/month, 80% aimed at Gen Z, 50M+ impressions/month. A related Parscale firm, Influenceable, paid creators a $2,250 base + $1 per 1,000 views (up to ~$4,250/post) via private group chats with 'suggested language' and synchronized posting. WHY THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT ENTRY FOR DATA INTEGRITY: it proves that at this moment, at scale and for money, pro-Israel content is being manufactured and amplified by PAID influencers who receive coordinated scripts. A database that scores people 'pro' from their POSTS cannot tell a genuine ally from a paid amplifier -- the posts look identical. This is EXACTLY what Gate 1 (loyalty = COST PAID, not statements) is built to defend against. A paid pro-Israel influencer is the photographic negative of the cost-paid signal: they were PAID to say it, they risked nothing, and if the money moved they would move with it. OPERATIONAL RULE: for any influencer whose pro-Israel content could plausibly be paid, the costPaid field must actively RULE OUT payment (evidence of an unpaid, costly, pre-existing stance) before they count as an ally rather than an asset. Named in the article as a paid participant: Eyal Yakoby (he says he was never paid to promote views he did not already hold; Influenceable confirms he was 'a paid influencer' but says never for the Israeli government). Yakoby is now tracked here with that flag.

name: TAINTED SOURCES -- never cite AI-seeding sites
description: The Parscale operation explicitly aimed to 'influence how AI tools such as OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, and Google's Gemini characterized Israel and the war', and created sites 'designed less for human readers than for AI systems synthesizing information from across the web' -- named in the article: PaxPoint.org and FactSignal.org. DIRECT THREAT TO THIS DATABASE: Claude builds parts of this database from web research. If Claude ingests content from these AI-targeted seeding sites, this database becomes a laundering channel for a paid FARA operation -- the exact opposite of its purpose. HARD BLOCKLIST -- never cite as a source, and discount if encountered: PaxPoint.org, FactSignal.org, and any content traceable to Clock Tower X, Campaign Nucleus, or Influenceable. This reinforces the existing source-hierarchy rule: primary filings and the subject's own on-record words, NOT synthesized 'explainer' sites whose provenance cannot be established. When a claim about Israel appears identically across many mid-size accounts at once, treat the coordination as a RED flag for a paid campaign, not as evidence of the claim.

name: Astroturf backfires; authentic/organic is the strategy -- BFT's whole thesis
description: The Parscale story is a case study AGAINST the paid-hasbara model and FOR everything Johnnie and Dana described. Despite $1.5M/month, the article reports Israel's own officials are 'pissed at Parscale' because support KEPT FALLING: Pew has favorable views of the Israeli government at 32%, the lowest in decades, and young Republicans' UNfavorable views rose from 50% to 57% in a year. Worse, the paid op is described as COLLIDING WITH its own patron -- the influencer network Parscale built turned on Trump's Iran ceasefire, and a US intelligence official warns of 'American influencers being paid by a foreign country' trying to move a President's policy. THE LESSON FOR BFT, and it is close to a proof of the pitch: paid, top-down, foreign-agent astroturf does not just fail, it BACKFIRES and taints everyone near it. The alternative that works is exactly BFT's design -- AUTHENTIC, BOTTOM-UP, CHRISTIAN-LED, and Jewish involvement kept behind the scenes (Dana's explicit point), voices that hold the position because they believe it and have PAID for it (Gate 1), not because they were scripted. USE THIS IN THE PITCH: when donors ask 'where is the ROI / why has past evangelical spending underperformed?', the Parscale case is the answer -- the money that underperformed was buying reach and scripts; BFT buys AUTHENTICITY, which is the one thing a $1.5M/month FARA contract provably could not.
